issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal-feeding method using two different names: the UML and many places specify an abstract method messageOnFeed(), but other places in the textual description (and instructions for Farm.feedAllAnimals()) refer to getFeedingSound(). This naming mismatch between messageOnFeed and getFeedingSound is likely to confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and template text to refer to messageOnFeed everywhere (matching the UML and the provided solution), or (B) change the UML and solution to use getFeedingSound consistently. Also update the Farm.feedAllAnimals() description and any example code to call the same method name so students know which abstract method to implement.

issues.description: The problem description uses getFeedingSound() when specifying the return values for each animal's feeding sound (e.g. "getFeedingSound() should return 'Arf Arf!'"), while the UML, template expectations, and the provided solution use the method name messageOnFeed(). This mismatch between getFeedingSound and messageOnFeed refers to the same conceptual operation (the animal's feeding sound) but uses two different identifiers, which can confuse students about which method they must implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Update the problem statement to refer to messageOnFeed() (replace getFeedingSound() occurrences), or alternatively add/mention a getFeedingSound() alias in the template/solution that delegates to messageOnFeed(). Preferably use messageOnFeed() throughout the problem text to match the UML and code.
